title: GCP Cloud Functions Retry and Error Rate Trending

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.5.15 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.5.15 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=gcp` sourcetype=`google:gcp:pubsub:message` collected via `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" resource.type="cloud_function"
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.15_gcp_cloud_functions_retr_15"
| sort -_time
description: Rising retries and error rates signal unstable dependencies or quota issues before quotas hard-stop traffic; trending supports SLO review and incident prevention.
value: Detecting gcp cloud functions retry and error rate trending early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Ingest execution count metrics with result/status labels from Cloud Monitoring. Supplement with log-based counts from Cloud Logging for detailed error classes. Baseline hourly error and retry rates per function. Alert when error share exceeds threshold or retries spike versus invocations.
visualization: Stacked area chart (executions by outcome), Line chart (error rate % over time), Table (function_name, invocations, errors, retry estimate).
knownFalsePositives: Inventories can skip a run when an API is throttled or a connector is in maintenance, which looks like a big drop. We check the ingest time and the last good snapshot before we call it shrinkage.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` with the modular input for `google:gcp:pubsub:message`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.5.16.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `messageId` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest execution count metrics with result/status labels from Cloud Monitoring. Supplement with log-based counts from Cloud Logging for detailed error classes. Baseline hourly error and retry rates per function. Alert when error share exceeds threshold or retries spike versus invocations.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:pubsub:message" resource.type="cloud_function"
| table _time messageId publishTime attributes
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.15_gcp_cloud_functions_retr_15"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:pubsub:message` in `index=gcp` to detect gcp cloud functions retry and error rate trending. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `messageId` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_5_15_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Stacked area chart (executions by outcome), Line chart (error rate % over time), Table (function_name, invocations, errors, retry estimate)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of gcp cloud functions retry and error rate trending so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
